topic.title: The offsite is cheaper than a raise
topic.claim: The team offsite in Goa costs the company less than one good raise, and makes you feel more seen than the raise would.
topic.moment: Matching t-shirts, a resort pool and a 'vision for next year' session after lunch.

turn.believed: Offsites are a perk or a waste of money.
turn.actually: They're a retention tool that works, and it's cheaper than paying people to stay.

topic.because: A raise is private and forgotten in two months. A trip with photos becomes a memory you tie to the team.
topic.payoff: The trip is real fun. Just notice which month it lands in, and whether it's near appraisals.
topic.behaviour: Companies fund trips, parties and swag while keeping increments tight.
topic.mechanism: A shared experience buys loyalty at a lower price than salary does.
topic.group: Employees at startups and mid-size firms
topic.send_to: The colleague still posting offsite photos while complaining about their hike.
topic.why_now: Year-end offsite season is about to start.
real_details: A post shared a Kaun Banega Crorepati clip where Amitabh Bachchan announces, with fake excitement, a 2-year ghee supply as the prize for answering 10 questions. Saif Ali Khan answers with equally ironic excitement.
A commenter worked out that a 2-year ghee supply costs about ₹17,280, assuming 1 litre a month at roughly ₹720 a litre.
Another commenter pointed out that the prize would also be taxable.
One person said their workplace rewards give 100 points worth ₹70, redeemable only as an Amazon voucher.

score.why: A Goa offsite is a cheaper retention tool than a raise, and he also admits the trip is genuinely fun.

topic.villain: a retention strategy that's cheaper than the raise it replaces
